hardware_summary: Two boilers aboard the FSRU Excellence (Excelerate Energy, IMO 9252539, built 2005), fired on boil-off gas, integral to the vessel's own power supply while moored and regasifying — a July 2026 fire that damaged the power/control cabling connected to those boilers forced a suspension/reduction of gas send-out, confirming the boilers (not shore power) run the terminal.
fuel_basis: Boil-off gas (BOG)-fired boilers/turbo-generation, the standard onboard fuel source for this vessel class (a steam-plant LNG carrier fitted as Excelerate's second LNGRV/FSRU in 2005); no source indicates diesel-only generation, and the vessel is moored offshore with no shore power connection.
captive_summary: Moheshkhali is served by Excelerate's FSRU Excellence, moored offshore (floating=True, offshore=True) with a subsea gas pipeline to shore but no shore power cable. The vessel's two boilers, run on boil-off gas, supply the FSRU's own electrical power for regasification pumps and other loads. A fire on 21 July 2026 'severely damaged critical power, control and instrumentation cables connected to its two boilers,' forcing a nationwide gas-supply cut of roughly 450 mmcfd while repairs (imported spare parts, UK/UAE technical teams) were arranged — direct evidence that the terminal's operation depends on the boilers' own power output rather than any external supply. No source discloses a specific MW rating for this vessel; general FSRU-conversion technical literature describes boil-off-gas-fired power plants in the 15-25 MW range built for exactly this purpose (running regasification units and other onboard loads).
confirmed_how: Two independent Bangladeshi outlets confirm the boiler-based power system's centrality: The Business Standard/tbsnews.net (28 July 2026): fire 'severely damaged critical power, control and instrumentation cables connected to its two boilers,' cutting supply by ~450 mmcfd. thereport.live (independently): the fire 'damag[ed] one of the terminal's two boilers and forc[ed] the facility to suspend operations.' The FSRU is permanently moored (not underway, so no propulsion draw), off-grid (subsea pipeline carries only gas to shore, no shore power documented), so per the standard off-grid FSRU prior it self-generates; general engineering background (industry technical write-ups on FSRU conversions) confirms boil-off-gas-fired boilers/engines in this class are sized 15-25 MW specifically to power regasification and other onboard loads. No primary vessel spec sheet (class society record, Excelerate technical datasheet) was found giving an exact MW figure for Excellence itself — that gap is why confidence is yellow rather than green, not a reason to withhold the YES per SOP (existence of on-site gas generation is documented; the missing MW figure is left blank).
